text:
Asha (People Ops): Hey team — quick Q: someone submitted a Lyft receipt but the photo is pretty blurry and Expensify OCR couldn't read the total. Passenger says fare was $42.10 incl tip. Do we accept a blurry photo + credit card statement screenshot, or do we need a rescan?
Liam: If the card txn matches the date & amount and the vendor is Lyft I usually approve. We require readable proof for amounts over $25 though.
Noah: Agreed. Policy is receipts preferred, but CC statement + annotation is acceptable for transport. We should ask for a short attestation sentence from the submitter for auditing.
Sabrina: I can approve if they attach the CC screenshot AND a short note like "I took Lyft on 3/12 from airport to hotel; total $42.10". Also prefer a map screenshot or trip receipt from the app if possible.
Asha (People Ops): Good — can you paste the exact wording we want them to use? I'll reply to the submitter.
Sabrina: Sure — ask them to add: "Trip on 2026-03-18, Lyft to/from SFO terminal A. Fare $42.10. Receipt image was blurry; attached card statement shows the charge. - [employee name]"
Liam: Also mention they should redact card numbers on the statement before uploading.
Noah: Expensify Bot can flag it as "needs attestation" so finance knows.
Expensify Bot: FYI: When you attach a supporting screenshot, use the file type JPEG/PNG. PDFs are fine but may slow OCR. Ensure filename includes the date, e.g., 2026-03-18-lyft.png.
Asha (People Ops): Perfect. I'll reply to the submitter with: "Can you please attach a screenshot of the card transaction (redact numbers), add a one-line attestation with the trip date/vendor/amount, and attach any in-app trip receipt or map screenshot? That will be sufficient for approval for ground transport. If we still can't verify, we'll need a short manager approval note"
Liam: One more nuance — international cards: if currency conversion shows a different USD amount on the statement, ask them to put both amounts in the attestation.
Sabrina: I'll add a quick blurb to the receipts wiki so anyone approving knows the workaround.
Asha (People Ops): Thanks — tagging @finance for awareness but will mark as resolved once the employee updates expense. :thumbsup:
